title: blackman
summary: Generate a Blackman window vector in MATLAB and RunMat.
description: `blackman` generates a Blackman window from a nonnegative scalar length. The length accepts single, double, or any of the eight built-in integer classes; floating lengths round to the nearest integer.
behaviors: `blackman(L)` returns an `L x 1` symmetric Blackman window.
`blackman(L, 'periodic')` returns the periodic form used in spectral-analysis workflows.
`blackman(..., 'single')` returns a single-precision window; `'double'` is the default.
Length `L` accepts single, double, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint8, uint16, uint32, or uint64; noninteger floating values round to the nearest integer.
A logical scalar length is available only as an explicitly gated RunMat extension.
For the symmetric case and `L > 1`, coefficients use `cospi` evaluation of `0.42 - 0.5*cospi(2*n/(L-1)) + 0.08*cospi(4*n/(L-1))`, matching the current enhanced-accuracy algorithm.
The periodic form is constructed by evaluating a symmetric window of length `L + 1` and dropping the final sample.

faqs.question: Why would I use `blackman` instead of `hann` or `hamming`?
faqs.answer: A Blackman window is often used when you want lower spectral leakage at the cost of a wider main lobe. It is a common tradeoff choice in spectral analysis workflows.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the symmetric and periodic Blackman window?
faqs.answer: Use the symmetric form for filter-design style workflows. Use `'periodic'` for FFT-based spectral analysis, where RunMat constructs a symmetric window of length `L + 1` and removes the final sample.

faqs.question: Does `blackman` support single precision?
faqs.answer: Yes. Pass `'single'` as the final option to request a single-precision output. The default output type is double precision.

faqs.question: Does an integer length produce an integer window?
faqs.answer: No. Every integer length class is a structural input; output is double by default or single when requested explicitly.

faqs.question: Does `blackman` accept a gpuArray input?
faqs.answer: No interactive gpuArray input form exists because the only numeric input is a host scalar length. GPU code generation is a separate documented capability; RunMat may internally materialize the new floating window on its active provider.
